name: lantern
description: A suite for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform developers who work across tenants: environments and app registrations, web resource, plug-in, PCF, and Power Pages deployment, Custom APIs, SQL and FetchXML queries, record inspection, plug-in traces and steps, metadata, and Dataverse-aware IntelliSense.
author: Nathan Brandt

enumDescriptions: VS Code's built-in Microsoft account sign-in.
Azure CLI (az account get-access-token). Use this if a client's tenant blocks the first option.
lantern.authMethod.description: How to sign in to the Dataverse Web API for web resource push and compare.

lantern.publishAfterPush.description: Publish web resources right after pushing them.

lantern.pushOnSave.description: Push web resources to Dataverse every time you save them. Only files whose web resource name is known for certain are pushed.

lantern.plugins.buildConfiguration.description: Build configuration used before pushing plug-ins.

lantern.pacPath.description: Path to the Power Platform CLI.

lantern.ilspyPath.description: Path to ILSpy's command-line decompiler (ilspycmd), used by Get Plug-in Source and Compare Deployed. Empty means ilspycmd on your PATH or in the .NET global tools folder; Lantern offers to install it.

lantern.azPath.description: Path to the Azure CLI (only for authMethod azureCli).

lantern.xrmDefinitelyTypedPath.description: Path to XrmDefinitelyTyped.exe. Empty means search tools/xdt in the workspace.

lantern.codeLens.enabled.description: Show Push/Compare links on web resources and Build and Push on plug-in classes.

lantern.metadata.completions.description: Suggest and describe column, control, tab, and section names inside getAttribute("…"), getControl("…"), tabs.get("…") and sections.get("…").

lantern.query.maxRows.description: Most rows a query returns before stopping (Dataverse sends 5,000 per page). Queries with TOP or aggregates aren't affected.

lantern.diagnostics.enabled.description: Show problems in form scripts as you type: columns that don't exist or aren't on any form, unknown controls, tabs, and sections, and form handlers the file doesn't define.

lantern.typescript.pushOnSave.description: When a TypeScript web resource is saved, compile it and push the .js output to Dataverse.

enumDescriptions: Use Lantern's global tenant storage across VS Code windows. Ignores local configuration files and requires tenant selection.
Use tenants in the folder's .lantern/config.json. The defaultTenant property selects one when the folder opens.
lantern.clientSettingsLocation.description: Where tenant settings (org, environments, solutions, accounts...) are kept. Storage modes are independent; switching does not move or delete configurations.

lantern.createJsconfig.description: Create a jsconfig.json in each local project folder for typed Xrm IntelliSense in form scripts. Lantern keeps it out of git through the repo's local exclude list.

lantern.mcp.enabled.markdownDescription: Run Lantern's MCP server on `127.0.0.1` so Claude Code, Codex and other MCP clients can use Lantern's tools (flow search, flow outlines, table descriptions, read-only queries). Set Up in **Lantern: AI Tools** turns this on. Copilot doesn't need it.

lantern.mcp.port.markdownDescription: Port for Lantern's MCP server. After changing it, run Set Up again for Claude Code (Codex follows automatically).

languageModelTools.name: lantern_tenants
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Shows the selected Dynamics 365 / Dataverse tenant, its org URL, environments, and solutions. Select a tenant in Lantern first.

languageModelTools.name: lantern_describe_table
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Describes a Dataverse table from a client's org: every column with its logical name, display name, type, required level, choice values, and lookup targets, plus each form and its event handlers. Use it before writing form scripts, plug-ins, or queries against the table.

table.description: Table logical name (like account) or display name.

languageModelTools.name: lantern_query
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs a read-only query against a client's Dataverse org and returns up to 50 rows as a table. Accepts a SQL SELECT (Lantern's dialect: SELECT [TOP n] columns FROM table [alias] [JOIN ... ON a.x = b.y] [WHERE ...] [GROUP BY ...] [HAVING ...] [ORDER BY ...], using logical names) or a FetchXML document. UPDATE, DELETE, and INSERT are refused. The person confirms each query before it runs.

query.description: A SQL SELECT statement or a FetchXML document.

languageModelTools.name: lantern_where_used
languageModelTools.displayName: Lantern: where a column is used
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Finds where a Dataverse column is used: on forms, in views, business rules and workflows, plug-in step filtering, and in the client folder's code (with the function each use is in). Use before renaming, removing, or changing a column.

languageModelTools.name: lantern_search_flows
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Finds Power Automate cloud flows in the selected tenant's environment by name, by what they do, or both. "uses" looks inside each flow's definition: one of the shortcuts email, teams, approval, http, sharepoint, childflow, dataverse-write (email finds every flow that sends email: Outlook, Mail, SendGrid, SMTP, Dataverse SendEmail), or any text (a table name, a connector like shared_sharepointonline, an action name, a URL). Returns each flow's ID, name, on/off state, solutions, and the steps that matched. Use lantern_explain_flow with an ID to see the whole flow.

uses.description: What the flow does: email, teams, approval, http, sharepoint, childflow, dataverse-write, or text to find in its definition (optional).

solution.description: Only flows in this solution (unique name, optional).

languageModelTools.name: lantern_explain_flow
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Outlines one Power Automate cloud flow from its definition so you can explain what it does: the trigger (table, change, filters, schedule), every step in order with its connector, operation and key parameters, conditions and loops with their expressions, and the connections it uses. Pass the flow's ID (from lantern_search_flows) or its name.

flow.description: The flow's ID, or its name.

languageModelTools.name: lantern_explain_plugin
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Outlines a Dataverse plug-in so you can explain what it does and when it runs: its assembly, display name and description, every registered step (message, table, stage, sync or async, order, enabled, filtering columns, pre/post images and their columns, run-as user, unsecure configuration), and its C# source when a project in the tenant folder builds it. Pass plugin (full or short class name, or display name) or assembly (assembly name, for every class in it). With neither, lists the registered assemblies.

plugin.description: Plug-in class: full type name, class name, or display name (optional).

languageModelTools.name: lantern_explain_web_resource
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Shows a Dataverse web resource so you can explain it: type, display name, description, solutions, and its deployed content (scripts, HTML, CSS, XML). For a JavaScript library, also the functions it defines and the forms that load it with the events each function handles (OnLoad, OnSave, OnChange of a column). Pass the full name (like acme_/scripts/account.js) or part of it.

name.description: Web resource name, or part of it.

languageModelTools.name: lantern_trace_column
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use when someone asks why a field behaves a certain way (gets a value, changes, is required, hidden, locked, or cleared). Gathers everything that can cause it: the column's definition (calculated, rollup or formula, required level, field security, autonumber, default), forms it's on and form events, deployed form-script lines that use it (setValue, setVisible, setRequiredLevel, setDisabled, ...) with the event that runs them, business rules and classic workflows, cloud flows that trigger on it or set it, plug-in steps that filter on it or can change it before save, and code in the tenant folder that mentions it. Then use lantern_explain_flow, lantern_explain_plugin or lantern_explain_web_resource on what looks responsible.

languageModelTools.name: lantern_generate_csharp_classes
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds tables and columns to the tenant's C# classes for plug-ins (one partial class per table, only the columns asked for). Use it when someone pastes a user story, spec, or ticket that lists the tables and fields a plug-in reads or writes: extract every table and column it mentions and pass them; display names ("Approval Status") or logical names (ohcp_approvalstatus) both work. It only adds: columns already in the classes or the queue are kept. By default the tables go into the C# classes queue in VS Code, shown in the status bar, for the person to review and generate; pass generate: true only when they asked for the files to be written now. Names it can't match come back with suggestions: check them with lantern_describe_table and call again with the logical names.

tables.description: Each table the story mentions, with the columns it needs.

table.description: Table logical name or display name, like ohcp_productrequest or Product Request.

columns.description: Column logical names or display names.

generate.description: Write the .cs files now instead of queueing them for review (default false).

namespace.description: C# namespace for the classes when generating (optional; empty for none).
